name: Pigeon Pea and Fenugreek Curry (Methi Tadka Dal)
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: 2 handfuls of methi leaves (only the leaves without the tender stem)
½ small spoon of mustard seeds

steps: Mix all above and put them in an Indian cooker (pressure cooker). Wait until the dal is cooked (4 whistles).
Heat the ghee in a pan, and add the mustard seeds, zheera, garlic, red chillies, and curry leaves. Fry until the garlic is golden.
Add the chopped tomato, salt, chilli powder, and coriander to taste.
Add the cooked dal mixture to the fried mixture, and let it simmer. You can add water if you like it to be more like gravy.
Add two drops of lemon juice for added taste.
Serve with hot rice, and an optional touch of Gongura pickle.

culture.text: Curry is a dish with a spicy sauce, initially in Indian cuisine, then modified by interchange with the Portuguese, followed by the British, and eventually thoroughly internationalised. Many curries are found in the cuisines of countries in Southeast Asia and East Asia.
